# Test fixtures

Everything here is generated by the float64 oracles in `tools/` and checked in. Never edit a
file by hand; regenerate and review the diff. License: all weights, goldens and op values are
synthetic (seeded pseudo-random numbers produced by the scripts in `tools/`), derived from no
model checkpoint and no third-party data; they carry the repository's own license. Only the
tensor NAMES and config KEYS follow the real Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 (Apache-2.0) checkpoints.

| fixture | generator | check |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen35-tiny/` | `python3 tools/make_tiny.py` | `python3 tools/make_tiny.py --check` |
| `gemma4-tiny/` | `python3 tools/make_tiny_gemma4.py` | `python3 tools/make_tiny_gemma4.py --check` |
| `ops/*.json` | `python3 tools/make_ops.py` | `python3 tools/make_ops.py --check` |

`--check` regenerates in memory and fails unless every file is byte-identical and no extra file is
present. Both generators are deterministic (seeded `random.Random`, no clocks, no environment).

## `qwen35-tiny/`

A complete Qwen3.5-shaped checkpoint small enough for unit tests. Seed 8 (constant `SEED` in
`tools/make_tiny.py`, found with `--find-seed`). About 1.5 MB.

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `config.json` | real schema: nested `text_config` (same keys, same order as the real 4B config), `model_type` `qwen3_5`, `layer_types`, `full_attention_interval` 4, `rope_parameters` (theta 1e7, partial_rotary_factor 0.25, mrope_section [2,1,1]); other top-level keys (`vision_config`, token ids) as in the real file |
| `model.safetensors-0000{1,2}-of-00002.safetensors` + `model.safetensors.index.json` | two shards, real tensor names with prefix `model.language_model.`. Shard 1: embedding and layers 0-3. Shard 2: layers 4-7, final norm, fake `model.visual.*` stubs (5 tensors; kept by the quantiser, never bound by the text engine) and `mtp.*` (3 tensors) |
| `model.q8.safetensors` | `tools/quant_ref.py` output for the dir above (format in the `quant_ref.py` docstring) |
| `golden_bf16.json`, `golden_q8.json` | oracle results, schema below |

Dimensions: 8 layers (indices 3 and 7 are full attention, the rest linear), hidden 64,
intermediate 128, vocab 384, 4 heads x 32 with 2 KV heads, rotary dim 8 (partial 0.25), linear
attention 2 key heads x 16 and 4 value heads x 16, conv kernel 4, eps 1e-6, tied embeddings.

dtypes: every tensor is BF16 (values exactly representable) EXCEPT
`...linear_attn.A_log`, which is F32, so both the BF16 and the F32 copy path are exercised. The
real checkpoint's dtype for `A_log` is not known to the oracle author; the engine should accept BF16
and F32 for `A_log`, `dt_bias` and the norms. Tensors: `conv1d.weight` is `[conv_dim, 1, 4]`.

Golden schema (compact JSON, one trailing newline):

```
{"tokens": [24 ints], "logits": [[384 floats] per token],
 "greedy": {"prompt": [first 8 of tokens], "out": [16 ints]}}
```

* `logits[t]` is the output at position t after feeding `tokens[0..t]` from a zero state.
  Floats are float64 oracle values printed with 9 significant digits (round-trips f32).
* `greedy.out` are the next 16 ids by argmax (lowest id wins ties), feeding each back.
* `golden_bf16.json`: weights from the shards. `golden_q8.json`: the oracle on the weights
  dequantised from `model.q8.safetensors` ((double)q * (double)scale), so both are exact targets.
* Margins, asserted by the generator for BOTH goldens: top-1 minus top-2 logit above 0.05 (plan asks
  for 1e-2) at all 24 positions and all 16 greedy steps (actual minima: bf16 0.100, q8 0.083); max
  |logit| about 19; gate tolerance 2e-4 * max|row| is about 4e-3; q8 and bf16 logits differ by up to 5.2.
* `lm-run --tokens <tokens> --logits-out F` must produce 24 rows; `--tokens <prompt> --greedy 16`
  must print `greedy.out`. `tools/check_golden.py` does exactly this.

## `gemma4-tiny/`

A complete Gemma 4 E4B-shaped text checkpoint (phase 2, `docs/PLAN.md`), generated by
`tools/make_tiny_gemma4.py` with the float64 oracle `tools/ref_gemma4.py`. Seed 16 (constant `SEED`,
found with `--find-seed`). About 2.6 MB. Same golden schema, q8 format and gate as `qwen35-tiny/`:
`python3 tools/check_golden.py --run bin/lm-run --quant bin/lm-quant --fixtures tests/fixtures/gemma4-tiny`
(the family is read from `config.json` `model_type`).

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `config.json` | real schema: top-level `model_type` `gemma4` with `audio_config`, `vision_config` and token ids (tiny stubs), nested `text_config` (same keys, same order as the real E4B config, `model_type` `gemma4_text`) |
| `model.safetensors` | ONE bf16 file (no index): all real text tensor names with prefix `model.language_model.` (including `layer_scalar` `[1]` and, for the four reuse layers 8-11, the unused `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `k_norm`), plus 8 tensors the engine MUST ignore: `model.vision_tower.*` (4, one a rank-0 scalar), `model.embed_vision.*`, `model.embed_audio.*`, `model.audio_tower.*` |
| `generation_config.json` | as the real file (`eos_token_id` [1, 106, 50]) |
| `model.q8.safetensors` | `tools/quant_ref.py` output (text and vision stubs, audio dropped; byte-identical when regenerated) |
| `golden_bf16.json`, `golden_q8.json` | oracle results, same schema as above |

Dimensions: 12 layers, `layer_types` 5 sliding + 1 full, twice (full at 5 and 11), hidden 64,
intermediate 128, 4 heads, 2 KV heads, `head_dim` 16 (sliding) and `global_head_dim` 32 (full),
`sliding_window` 8, `num_kv_shared_layers` 4 (layers 8-11 reuse; the producers are layer 7 for sliding
and layer 5 for full), `hidden_size_per_layer_input` **32**, vocab 384 for both vocab sizes, eps 1e-6,
tied embeddings, rope: sliding default theta 1e4, full proportional theta 1e6 with partial 0.25
(4 rotated pairs of 16). `final_logit_softcapping` 16. All tensors are BF16 (values exactly representable).

Deviation from `docs/PLAN.md`: the plan says `hidden_size_per_layer_input` 8. `per_layer_projection`
is `[hidden, P]` and the q8 format needs every quantised input dimension to be a multiple of 32, so
P = 8 cannot be quantised; 32 is the smallest working value (`per_layer_input_gate` is `[P, hidden]`,
`embed_tokens_per_layer` `[384, 12*32]`, `per_layer_model_projection` `[384, 64]`).

Golden: `tokens` has 40 ids (more than 2 x window), `greedy.prompt` is the first 20 (also more than
2 x window), `greedy.out` 16 ids. Margins asserted by the generator for BOTH goldens: top-1 minus top-2
logit above 0.03 at all 40 positions and 16 greedy steps (actual minima: bf16 0.0395, q8 0.0440; the
gate tolerance 2e-4 * max|logit| is 1.9e-3, so the gap is 20x the tolerance); at least 8 distinct argmax
ids over the positions and 4 distinct greedy ids; the softcap bites (max pre-cap |logit| 12.5 >=
cap/2 = 8; capped max 9.73 < 16); q8 and bf16 logits differ by up to 1.2 (3x the tolerance is required);
with the sliding window switched off the logits change by up to 12.8, so the mask is visible in the
golden. bf16 and q8 agree on the argmax at 36 of 40 positions and on the first 8 greedy ids. The model
is built so `layer_scalar` in [0.5, 1.5] (bf16) and the norms are plain-weight (about 1, not about 0).

## `qwen35-vl-tiny/`

The Qwen3.5 image encoder (docs/PLAN.md "Phase 3"). Generated by `tools/make_tiny_vl.py` (`--check`
regenerates in memory and compares) with the float64 oracle `tools/ref_vision_qwen35.py`, which was
checked once against transformers' `Qwen3_5VisionModel` (float64, eager attention) on these weights:
largest difference 1.6e-7 of max|row| (transformers runs softmax and the rope table in float32).
About 1.8 MB. Gate: `check_golden.py ... --fixtures tests/fixtures/qwen35-vl-tiny` (check 5).

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `config.json` | the `qwen35-tiny` config with a real small `vision_config` |
| `model.safetensors` | ONE bf16 file: the `qwen35-tiny` text and MTP tensors (its visual stubs left out) and a complete `model.visual.*` encoder; the patch embedding is the checkpoint's 5-D Conv3d weight |
| `model.q8.safetensors` | `tools/quant_ref.py` output: every vision matrix is q8 (the 5-D weight flattened to `[32, 1536]`), `pos_embed.weight` included |
| `img_64x64.ppm`, `img_64x96.ppm`, `img_32x32.ppm` | P6 test images at grid size (gradient plus noise): 4, 6 and 1 tokens |
| `golden_vision_bf16.json`, `golden_vision_q8.json` | `{"images":[{"image","height","width","rows"}]}`: the oracle's encoder output per image, rows as `%.9g` |

Vision dimensions: depth 2, hidden 32, 2 heads (`head_dim` 16), intermediate 64, patch 16, merge 2,
temporal 2, 16 position embeddings (a 4x4 table, so every image interpolates it), out 64 (the text
hidden size). Seed `VISION_SEED` 1. Margins asserted by the generator: no two rows of an image equal;
q8 and bf16 rows differ by at least 92x the gate tolerance (3x is required). No text goldens yet
(phase 2 adds image-conditioned logits).

## `gemma4-vl-tiny/`

The Gemma 4 image encoder and `embed_vision`. Same generator (`tools/make_tiny_vl.py --family gemma4`),
oracle `tools/ref_vision_gemma4.py`, checked once against transformers' `Gemma4VisionModel` plus
`Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder` (float64, eager): largest difference 8.5e-7 of max|row|. About 2.6 MB.
Same files and golden schema as `qwen35-vl-tiny/`; the text part is the `gemma4-tiny` model (its
vision stubs left out, its audio stubs kept, which the quantiser drops).

Vision dimensions: 2 layers, hidden 32, 2 query heads over 1 KV head (`head_dim` 16), intermediate
64, patch 16, pooling 3, a 16-entry position table per axis, clipped linears on (bounds drawn in
+-[1, 2.5]), out 64. Images 48x48, 96x144 and 144x96 (1, 6 and 6 tokens). Seed `GEMMA_VISION_SEED` 1.
Margins asserted: no two rows of an image equal; q8 and bf16 rows differ by at least 154x the gate
tolerance; turning the clamps off changes the rows by more than 3x the tolerance.

The tiny vocab is 384, so `boi_token_id` / `image_token_id` / `eoi_token_id` in this fixture are
11 / 12 / 13 (in-range stand-ins). Pad stays 0. The engine reads those ids from the config; a real
checkpoint keeps 255999 / 258880 / 258882. `golden_image_bf16.json` and `golden_image_q8.json` are
the text logits after an image block:

```
{"blocks":[{"image","prefix":[ints],"logits":[384 floats]}]}
```

`logits` is the next-token row after the prefix and then `<boi>`, one position per encoder row,
`<eoi>`. Positions increase by one and attention stays causal. At the encoder rows the residual is
the vision row (not scaled by the text embedding scale) and the per-layer table lookup is the pad
id; the projection is of the vision row. Two blocks: `img_96x144.ppm` with prefix `[3,15,17,2]`
(6 image tokens) and `img_48x48.ppm` with prefix `[5]` (1 image token). Margins: argmax gap above
3x the gate tolerance; q8 logits differ from bf16 by more than 3x; swapping the pad id for the
image-token id in the per-layer table, or replacing the vision rows with the scaled pad embedding,
moves the bf16 logits by more than 3x. `lm-run [--tokens PREFIX] --image IMG --logits-out F` must
produce that one row. `check_golden.py` does this (check 6) on top of the encoder rows (check 5).

## `ops/*.json`

Compact JSON, one file per op. All activations are f32-exact, all weights bf16-exact; expected
outputs are float64 (a C test with f32 math should compare with about
`1e-5 * max(1, max|y|)`; the q8 file is exact). Every file has `"op"` and `"formula"` or `"note"`.

* `rmsnorm.json`: `eps`, `cases` of `{x[n], w[n], y[n]}`. `y = x * rsqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) * (1+w)`.
  n in 1, 7, 16, 33, 64, 256; one all-zero x; one tiny x (1e-4 scale).
* `rmsnorm_gated.json`: `eps`, `cases` of `{x, z, w, y}`; `y = x * rsqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) * w * silu(z)`.
  `w` is PLAIN (no `1+`).
* `l2norm.json`: `eps` 1e-6, `cases` of `{x, y}`, `y = x * rsqrt(sum(x^2)+eps)`; includes zero and tiny x.
* `rope.json`: `groups` of `{head_dim, rot_dim, theta, cases:[{pos, x[head_dim], y[head_dim]}]}`.
  Rotate-half on the first `rot_dim` entries, the rest unchanged. Groups: 32/8/1e7 (positions up to
  4093), 256/64/1e7 (real shape, positions up to 100000), 16/16/100, 24/6/10000.
* `conv1d_silu.json`: `cases` of `{channels, kernel, weight[channels][kernel], x[T][channels],
  y[T][channels], split, state_at_split[kernel-1][channels]}`. Causal depthwise conv then SiLU, zero
  initial state; `weight[c][kernel-1]` multiplies the current input. `state_at_split` holds the
  `kernel-1` inputs before position `split` (oldest first): starting a fresh run at `x[split:]` with
  that state must give `y[split:]`.
* `gated_delta_rule.json`: `cases` of `{num_k_heads, num_v_heads, dk, dv, steps:[{q[nk*dk], k[nk*dk],
  v[nv*dv], g[nv], beta[nv], o[nv*dv]}], final_state[nv][dk][dv]}`. `q`, `k` are the RAW post-conv
  values: the op applies `l2norm(eps 1e-6)` per key head and scales `q` by `1/sqrt(dk)`. `g` is the
  already computed log-decay (<= 0), `beta` the already computed sigmoid. Value head `i` uses key head
  `i / (nv/nk)` (consecutive). State `S[dk][dv]` starts at zero. Cases: 2x4 heads 16/16 (10 steps),
  1x3 heads 8/12 (6 steps), 2x2 heads (5 steps).
* `full_attention_layer.json`: `{hidden 32, heads 4, kv_heads 2, head_dim 16, rot_dim 8, theta 100, eps,
  weights, x[8][32], y[8][32]}`. Mixer only (no residual, no input norm; `x` is already normed).
  `weights` keys are `q_proj.weight` `[heads*head_dim*2][hidden]` (per head: query rows then gate rows),
  `k_proj.weight`, `v_proj.weight` `[kv_heads*head_dim][hidden]`, `o_proj.weight` `[hidden][heads*head_dim]`,
  `q_norm.weight`, `k_norm.weight` `[head_dim]`. Includes per-head q/gate split, q_norm/k_norm,
  partial RoPE at position t for `x[t]`, causal GQA softmax attention, sigmoid output gate.
* `linear_attention_layer.json`: `{hidden 32, num_k_heads 2, num_v_heads 4, key_head_dim 8,
  value_head_dim 8, conv_kernel 4, eps, weights, x[8][32], y[8][32]}`. Mixer only. `weights`:
  `in_proj_qkv.weight`, `in_proj_z.weight`, `in_proj_b.weight`, `in_proj_a.weight`, `conv1d.weight`
  (`[conv_dim][kernel]`, the `[C,1,K]` tensor squeezed), `dt_bias`, `A_log`, `norm.weight` (plain,
  `[value_head_dim]`), `out_proj.weight`. Zero conv and recurrent state before `x[0]`.
* `mlp.json`: `{hidden 32, intermediate 48, weights{gate_proj.weight, up_proj.weight,
  down_proj.weight}, x[4][32], y[4][32]}`, `y = down(silu(gate(x)) * up(x))`.
* `q8_quantize.json`: `{group 32, groups:[{name, x[32], x_bf16_bits[32], scale, scale_f32_bits, q[32]}],
  matrix:{rows 3, cols 96, x[288], q[288], scale[9], scale_f32_bits[9]}}`. Groups: `ties_at_half_scale_1`
  (scale exactly 1.0, ties at .5 round to even), `zero_group`, `negative_zero_group`,
  `negative_zero_with_values`, `max_negative_at_clamp`, `max_positive_at_clamp`, `scale_not_exact`,
  `tiny_values`, `bf16_subnormal_scale` (scale is an f32 subnormal: no flush-to-zero),
  `huge_values`, `random_0..5`. `matrix` row-major `[rows][cols]`, scales `[rows][cols/32]`, the third
  group of row 0 is all zero (scale 0).

Floating point in these files is Python `repr`, which round-trips doubles exactly.

### Gemma ops (`ops/gemma_rmsnorm.json` and friends)

Same conventions as above (f32-exact activations, bf16-exact weights, float64 expected values). They
come from a separate RNG stream (`GEMMA_SEED`), so adding them did not change any earlier file.

* `gemma_rmsnorm.json`: `eps`, `cases` of `{x, w, y}`, `y = x * (mean(x^2)+eps)^(-1/2) * w` (PLAIN `w`,
  not `1 + w`; includes an all-zero x and a 1e-4-scale x), and `cases_noweight` of `{x, y}` (`v_norm`: w = 1).
* `gelu_tanh.json`: `cases` of `{x[], y[]}`, `y = 0.5x(1 + tanh(sqrt(2/pi)(x + 0.044715x^3)))`; includes
  0, +-1e-8, +-0.5, +-1, +-3, +-6, +-10, +-30, +-100 and random values.
* `gelu_tanh_mul.json`: `cases` of `{gate[], up[], y[]}`, `y = gelu_tanh(gate) * up` (the MLP product).
* `gemma_rope.json`: `groups` of `{head_dim, rope_type, theta, partial_rotary_factor, freqs[head_dim/2],
  cases:[{pos, x[head_dim], y[head_dim]}]}`. Rotate-half over the whole head (pairs `i`, `i + d/2`),
  angle `pos * freqs[i]`. `default`: `freqs[i] = theta^(-2i/d)`. `proportional`: `r = int(partial*d/2)`,
  `freqs[i] = theta^(-2i/d)` (denominator `d`, not `2r`) for `i < r`, else 0, so dims `i >= r` pass
  through. Groups: default 16/1e4 and 256/1e4 (the real sliding shape), proportional 32/1e6/0.25,
  512/1e6/0.25 (the real full shape) and 16/100/0.5. Positions include 0, 1, 511, 512, 4096, 4093,
  100000 and 131071.
* `logit_softcap.json`: `cases` of `{cap, x[], y[]}`, `y = cap * tanh(x / cap)`; caps 30, 12, 1; includes
  +-cap, +-10*cap, +-1000 and values near 0.
* `sliding_attention.json`: `scaling` 1.0, `cases` of `{heads, kv_heads, head_dim, window (null = plain
  causal), pos, first_visible, q[heads*d], k[pos+1][kv_heads*d], v[pos+1][kv_heads*d], y[heads*d]}`.
  One query at position `pos` (q, k, v already normed and roped); it sees keys `j` with
  `first_visible <= j <= pos`, i.e. `j > pos - window`; scores are `q.k` with no `1/sqrt(d)`; head `h` uses
  KV head `h / (heads / kv_heads)`; `y` is the per-head context before `o_proj`. Cases: window 8 at pos
  0, 5, 7 (all keys visible), 8 (key 0 is exactly `pos - window`, excluded) and 20 (more than 2 x window);
  GQA 8/2 (window 4), MHA 4/4 (window 3), window 1, and `window: null` with head_dim 32. A ring cache of
  the last `min(window, pos+1)` rows must give the same `y`.
